notes.title: Integration by Parts and Taylor Series
notes.content:
# Integration by Parts & Series Expansions

## 1. Integration by Parts Formula
Derived from the product rule of differentiation:
$$\int u \, dv = u v - \int v \, du$$

### LIATE Priority Rule for Choosing u:
1. Logarithmic functions (ln x)
2. Inverse trigonometric functions (arctan x)
3. Algebraic polynomial powers (x^2, x^3)
4. Trigonometric functions (sin x, cos x)
5. Exponential functions (e^x)

## 2. Taylor Series Definition
The Taylor series expansion of a smooth infinitely differentiable function f(x) centered at a is:
$$f(x) = \sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{f^{(n)}(a)}{n!} (x - a)^n$$

When a = 0, this is termed the Maclaurin Series.

notes.title: Newton's Laws and Conservation of Momentum
notes.content:
# Newtonian Mechanics & Conservation Principles

## Newton's Three Axioms:
1. First Law (Inertia): A body remains at rest or in uniform linear motion unless acted upon by a net external force.
2. Second Law (Force & Acceleration): Force equals the time rate of change of momentum:
$$\vec{F}_{net} = \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt} = m \vec{a}$$
3. Third Law (Action-Reaction): For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction:
$$\vec{F}_{A \to B} = -\vec{F}_{B \to A}$$

## Conservation of Linear Momentum:
In an isolated system with no external net forces, total linear momentum is conserved:
$$\sum \vec{p}_{initial} = \sum \vec{p}_{final}$$
Elastic collisions conserve both kinetic energy and linear momentum.
